title: Reverse UPI 'Collect Request' Refund Scam
situation: A user selling furniture online receives a call from a buyer who promises to pay via UPI. Instead of sending money, the buyer sends a UPI 'Collect Request' for Rs 15,000, claiming the seller must approve it to receive the advance.
how_works: Fraudsters exploit the misunderstanding between 'Send' and 'Receive' in UPI apps. They initiate a debit collect request. If the victim enters their UPI MPIN, money is debited immediately from their account.
warning_signs: Receiving a request that asks for your UPI PIN; caller repeatedly saying 'Enter PIN to accept money'; urgency and pressure on call.
manipulation: Confusion of technical terms, claiming bank policy requires PIN verification for receiving merchant transfers.
victim_actions: Decline the collect request immediately; block the caller; check account statement; notify bank if clicked.
avoid_actions: Never enter your UPI PIN to receive money under any circumstances. UPI PIN is solely for authorising debits.
risk_reduction: Remember the cardinal rule: 'No PIN is required to receive money in UPI'. Set daily transaction limits.
reporting_guidance: Report caller on National Cyber Crime Portal (cybercrime.gov.in) and call 1930 within the golden hour.
tags: UPI, Collect Request, MPIN, Online Selling

title: Screen Sharing App Remote UPI Theft (AnyDesk/TeamViewer)
situation: A bank customer facing failed transaction issues calls a number found online. The 'executive' instructs them to install QuickSupport or AnyDesk to resolve the pending refund.
how_works: The fraudster asks the victim to read out the 9-digit remote access code. Once connected, they watch the victim open their banking app and type their credentials and MPIN, capturing full screen contents and session tokens.
warning_signs: Request to install remote desktop utilities (AnyDesk, TeamViewer, RustDesk); asking for 9-digit session code.
manipulation: Fake empathy, official sounding jargon ('diagnostic verification', 'screen mirror protocol').
victim_actions: Disconnect internet immediately, uninstall the remote tool, change netbanking and UPI passwords from another phone.
avoid_actions: Do not allow screen sharing with unknown persons; never open banking apps while a remote session is running.
risk_reduction: Do not search for customer care numbers on public search engines; only use official bank apps or physical passbook.
reporting_guidance: Call bank customer care to freeze accounts, report to cybercrime.gov.in and dial 1930.
tags: Remote Access, AnyDesk, Screen Share, UPI Theft

title: Fake Payment Confirmation Screenshot Scam
situation: A shopkeeper is shown a realistic-looking Google Pay/PhonePe screenshot on the customer's phone showing 'Rs 4,500 Paid Successfully'. The customer rushes away before the merchant's soundbox confirms payment.
how_works: Fraudsters use spoof payment generator apps that simulate transaction success screens with animated ticks, fake UTR numbers, and merchant names, while no actual bank transfer occurs.
warning_signs: No SMS confirmation received on merchant phone; Soundbox did not announce payment; customer is overly impatient.
manipulation: Creating artificial hurry, claiming network lag on merchant's phone, feigning distress or bus schedule urgency.
victim_actions: Do not release goods until your own soundbox or bank SMS/app registers the credit. Note vehicle/person details.
avoid_actions: Never accept visual phone screenshots as proof of funds transfer.
risk_reduction: Rely exclusively on audio soundbox notifications or direct SMS from your banking provider.
reporting_guidance: Report the fake transaction attempt to local police cyber cell and market association.
tags: Fake Screenshot, Spoof UPI, Soundbox, Retail Scam

title: Overpayment and Return via UPI Trap
situation: A person receives an SMS claiming Rs 50,000 has been accidentally credited to their bank account by a stranger. Moments later, a weeping caller begs for Rs 45,000 to be returned immediately for medical treatment.
how_works: The scammer sends a spoofed SMS styled like a bank notification, or uses a stolen bank account to initiate a fraudulent transfer that will soon be reversed by the real victim's bank, leaving the second victim with a net loss.
warning_signs: SMS originates from a random 10-digit mobile number rather than an official bank sender ID (e.g., AD-HDFCBK); immediate emotional phone call.
manipulation: Emotional manipulation, invoking medical emergencies, dying relatives, or severe panic.
victim_actions: Log into your bank app independently to check true account balance; do not refund any money directly; ask caller to contact their bank.
avoid_actions: Never refund disputed funds directly via UPI. Tell the caller to initiate an official bank-to-bank reversal.
risk_reduction: Educate family members on checking official bank statements rather than relying on SMS alerts alone.
reporting_guidance: Inform your bank branch manager in writing about the unverified credit and notify 1930.
tags: Overpayment, Accidental Transfer, Social Engineering, UPI

title: SIM Swap Attack on Netbanking Authentication
situation: A user suddenly notices 'No Service' on their mobile network. Within an hour, multiple unauthorized IMPS transfers drain their savings account while they struggle to get signal.
how_works: Scammers obtain the victim's personal details and ID copy, file a fraudulent SIM replacement with the telecom provider, and gain access to the physical number to receive SMS OTPs for banking resets.
warning_signs: Sudden, unexplained loss of mobile network signal; multiple missed calls from unknown foreign numbers preceding signal loss.
manipulation: Distracting the victim with nuisance calls so they turn off their phone or ignore network disappearance.
victim_actions: Immediately contact telecom provider from another phone to report unauthorized SIM swap; contact bank to lock netbanking.
avoid_actions: Do not ignore unexpected loss of cellular service, especially if netbanking credentials were recently compromised.
risk_reduction: Upgrade to telecom e-SIM with PIN protection; register email-based secondary alerts with your bank.
reporting_guidance: Dial 1930 immediately to freeze transactions in the banking switch before fraudsters cash out.
tags: SIM Swap, Netbanking, OTP Interception, Telecom

title: Credit Card Limit Enhancement Phishing Call
situation: A caller impersonating the bank's credit card department offers a free upgrade to 'Platinum Card' with double credit limit and zero annual fee, asking the customer to confirm the 16-digit card number and CVV.
how_works: The scammer uses leaked card databases to quote partial details, building false trust, then asks for expiry date, CVV, and the OTP sent by the bank, which is actually authorizing an international e-commerce purchase.
warning_signs: Caller asking for CVV, card expiry date, or OTP; promises of miraculous free limit upgrades without formal application.
manipulation: False authority, claiming the offer expires at midnight or is a special loyalty reward.
victim_actions: Refuse to provide CVV or OTP; disconnect the call; open the official bank mobile application to manage card limits securely.
avoid_actions: Never disclose CVV, card PIN, or transaction OTP to anyone, including bank representatives.
risk_reduction: Enable transaction limits, disable international usage, and turn off contactless payments when not in use.
reporting_guidance: Block the card immediately using the bank mobile app and report the incident to 1930.
tags: Credit Card, CVV, Limit Upgrade, Phishing

title: Electricity Bill Disconnection Threat SMS
situation: An SMS arrives at 8 PM: 'Dear customer, your electricity will be disconnected tonight at 9:30 PM due to unpaid previous month bill. Contact power officer at 9876543210 immediately.'
how_works: When the anxious victim calls, the fraudster impersonates an electricity board official, claiming system error, and asks them to download a Rs 10 recharge APK or open a payment link, resulting in device compromise.
warning_signs: Late evening SMS threatening immediate power cut; personal 10-digit mobile number provided for customer support.

victim_actions: Do not call the mobile number. Check electricity bill status on official state electricity distribution portal or consumer bill.
avoid_actions: Do not download any APK files sent via WhatsApp or SMS to resolve utility bills.
risk_reduction: Official electricity disconnections are never executed through personal mobile numbers on 1-hour notice without written prior notices.
reporting_guidance: Report the mobile number on Sanchar Saathi's Chakshu portal and dial 1930.
tags: Electricity Bill, Disconnection, Utility Scam, APK Malware

title: ATM Card Skimming and Shimming
situation: A customer uses an ATM kiosk at a quiet location. Two days later, unauthorized cash withdrawals take place across another state.
how_works: Criminals install thin magnetic stripe skimmers or microchip shimmers in the ATM card slot, paired with a hidden pinhole camera or fake keypad overlay to record the ATM PIN.
warning_signs: Loose or unusually bulky card reader bezel; misaligned keypad; glue residue around ATM card slot.
manipulation: Targeting poorly lit, unguarded standalone ATM booths during holiday weekends.
victim_actions: Cover the keypad with your free hand while typing PIN; report suspicious ATM machines to bank security immediately.
avoid_actions: Do not use ATMs where the card reader seems loose, damaged, or exhibits blinking lights of odd colors.
risk_reduction: Prefer bank branch on-site ATMs; switch to contactless cash withdrawal via UPI at supported ATMs.
reporting_guidance: Call bank customer support immediately to block ATM card and dispute fraudulent withdrawals.
tags: ATM Skimming, Shimming, PIN Theft, Banking

title: Fake Income Tax Refund Phishing SMS
situation: During tax season, a taxpayer gets an SMS: 'Your Income Tax Refund of Rs 24,490 has been approved. Submit your bank account details here to receive within 2 hours: http://incometax-efiling-refund.in'.
how_works: The phishing website replicates the Income Tax e-Filing portal, prompting the user for PAN, Aadhaar, Netbanking login credentials, and card details, which are harvested instantly.
warning_signs: Refund amount ending in odd numbers to look genuine; shortened or unofficial domain names; SMS from private phone numbers.
manipulation: Greed and excitement of getting a tax refund from the government.
victim_actions: Do not click the link. Log in directly to the official Income Tax portal (incometax.gov.in) to check refund status.
avoid_actions: Never submit netbanking passwords or debit card details to receive any government refund.
risk_reduction: Income Tax department always credits refunds directly to pre-validated bank accounts without external third-party links.
reporting_guidance: Forward phishing SMS to incident@cert-in.org.in and webmanager@incometax.gov.in.
tags: Income Tax, Tax Refund, Phishing, Government Impersonation

title: Pre-Approved Loan Processing Fee Scam
situation: A person receives an SMS or WhatsApp message: 'Pre-approved loan of Rs 5,00,000 at 2% interest. No income proof required. Pay Rs 2,500 file processing charge to disburse.'
how_works: The scammer sends fake loan sanction letters with forged RBI or bank logos. Once the victim pays the initial processing fee, new demands emerge for GST, insurance, and clearance fees until the victim stops paying.
warning_signs: Unrealistic low interest rates without credit verification; demanding upfront processing fees into personal savings accounts.
manipulation: Exploiting urgent financial distress, medical debt, or poor credit scores.
victim_actions: Stop all communication; do not transfer any processing fees; demand physical branch verification.
avoid_actions: Never pay upfront fees to secure a loan. Legitimate financial institutions deduct processing fees from disbursed amounts.
risk_reduction: Verify all lenders on the RBI List of Registered NBFCs and Banks before engaging.
reporting_guidance: Lodge an official complaint with the local cybercrime cell and at cybercrime.gov.in.
tags: Pre-Approved Loan, Processing Fee, Advance Fee, Fraud

title: Biometric AePS (Aadhaar Enabled Payment System) Skimming
situation: A rural resident discovers that funds were withdrawn from their bank account through AePS without their knowledge, even though their ATM card and phone were in their pocket.
how_works: Criminals acquire cloned silicone fingerprint replicas obtained from registry offices or property documents, using them on AePS micro-ATMs to withdraw cash up to daily limits.
warning_signs: Unauthorized SMS alerts showing AePS cash withdrawal; no physical card or OTP was requested.
manipulation: Exploiting trusting citizens who frequently leave thumb impressions on public deeds or unverified kiosks.
victim_actions: Immediately open the UIDAI mAadhaar app or website and 'Lock Biometrics' feature to prevent further AePS debits.
avoid_actions: Do not leave unprotected photocopies of Aadhaar cards with full numbers visible; use Masked Aadhaar.
risk_reduction: Keep biometric lock enabled in the UIDAI portal; unlock only momentarily when you personally need to authenticate.
reporting_guidance: Lodge an urgent complaint with your bank's fraud monitoring cell and report to 1930.
tags: AePS, Aadhaar, Biometric Skimming, UIDAI

title: Cheque Kiting and Positive Pay System Evasion
situation: A business owner writes a vendor cheque of Rs 15,000. Scammers intercept the physical cheque in transit, use chemical wash to alter payee name and amount to Rs 4,50,000, and present it for clearing.
how_works: Chemical alteration of physical cheques to change beneficiary details and amounts, targeting high balance business accounts.
warning_signs: Discrepancies in monthly bank statement; clearing alerts for unexpected high amounts.
manipulation: Exploiting delays in physical delivery and non-utilization of bank safety mandates.
victim_actions: Immediately notify bank branch manager to recall clearing; file police FIR for cheque interception and forgery.
avoid_actions: Never issue high-value cheques without registering details in the bank's Positive Pay System (PPS).
risk_reduction: Use permanent indelible ink; write 'A/C Payee' clearly; register Positive Pay details with your bank for any cheque above Rs 50,000.
reporting_guidance: File complaint with bank grievance redressal officer and local economic offences wing.
tags: Cheque Forgery, Positive Pay, Chemical Wash, Business Scam
